metadata.case_name: CHANG TSUN TEIN v. WAI LEE SCAFFOLDING CO LTD

source: According to the hospital report, Mr. Chang had a 2cm laceration of the scalp, with no neurological deficit.
injuries.icd_description: Laceration without foreign body of head

injuries.description: 4 cm scar over the left high parietal region
source: He was recorded to be conscious and alert, with a 4 cm scar over the left high parietal region.
Mr. Chang had a mild head injury as a result of the accident.
Dr. Woo considered that Mr. Chang's residual headache, dizziness, and subjectively impaired memory are consistent with the diagnosis of a very mild post-concussional syndrome.

injuries.description: adjustment disorder with mixed anxiety and depressive mood
source: Dr. Ho diagnosed Mr. Chang as suffering from a very mild degree of post-concussional disorder, and adjustment disorder with mixed anxiety and depressive mood.

injuries.description: moderate degree of post-traumatic stress disorder
source: Dr. Chen diagnosed Mr. Chang as suffering from a moderate degree of post-traumatic stress disorder, with impairment in his cognitive function.
Dr. Chen diagnosed Mr. Chang as suffering from a moderate degree of post-traumatic stress disorder, with impairment in his cognitive function.

manifestations.description: impairment in psychological and social functioning
hearing a female voice calling him at night
mild to moderate degree of cognitive deficit (mini-mental test 20/30)

treatments_received: treated with Panadol and discharged on the same day
referred to the neurosurgery clinic for management of suspected post-concussion syndrome
seen by the psychiatrist for poor sleep and was put on medication
neuro-psychological assessment by the clinical psychologist of the Castle Peak Hospital
psychiatric/psychological outpatient treatment once every 3 or 4 months
treatments_future: further psychological treatment (to be provided by government hospitals)

losses.description: inability to concentrate, loss of memory and impairment in cognitive function
4 cm scar over the left high parietal region
impairment in psychological and social functioning; social withdrawal / unsociable behaviour

Dr. Ho diagnosed Mr. Chang as suffering from a very mild degree of post-concussional disorder, and adjustment disorder with mixed anxiety and depressive mood. Dr. Chen diagnosed Mr. Chang as suffering from a moderate degree of post-traumatic stress disorder, with impairment in his cognitive function.
